files.purpose: The full marketing home page for getdroppycode.app: a single static, no-build-step HTML document (UTF-8, CRLF line endings) presenting Droppy Code as the supercharged coding agent for Mac. Its leading HTML comment states it is the dark sibling of getdroppy.app reusing the same notch dock, reveal motion, highlight rail, pinned wordscroll and footer, re-tokened for a code canvas, and that every picture and film of the app is the real app rendered by scripts/website_captures.py from the app's own capture mode with mock data, encoded at 2x and served from R2 under site-assets/droppy-code.

state_owned: sessionStorage key 'droppyCodeNavIntro' - the inline head script reads it: if present it appends the class ' nav-intro-done' to documentElement, otherwise it sets the key to '1'. So the nav intro animation plays only once per browser session. The whole thing is wrapped in try/catch so blocked storage does not break the page.
documentElement class 'nav-intro-done' - the only DOM state this file itself mutates
Initial ARIA state the scripts later toggle: aria-expanded='false' on .nav__menu and on all eleven .faq__question buttons, aria-current='true' on the first highlight slide, disabled on the prev arrow
side_effects: sessionStorage.getItem and sessionStorage.setItem('droppyCodeNavIntro') in a render-blocking inline head script placed before the stylesheets
Cross-origin font fetches to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (two preconnects plus one stylesheet link)
Cross-origin media fetches to droppy-releases.jordylegrand.workers.dev for every product screenshot
Hero image loads with loading='eager' decoding='async' fetchpriority='high'; every other image uses loading='lazy' decoding='async'
No analytics, telemetry, cookie banner or third-party tracking script is present anywhere in the document

feature_notes: Cache-busting query strings pin asset versions: site.css?v=14, wordscroll.css?v=5, site.js?v=5, wordscroll.js?v=5, code.js?v=7, og-home.png?v=2
Screenshot generations are versioned in the CDN path: tour/v5/ for the app tour images and usage/v1/ for the limits shot
The advertised shipping version is 1.5.3, 'Signed and notarized'
The page states '10 agent providers' in the stats and 'Ten providers' in the outro, while the agents grid renders twelve marks and the footer description lists eleven (it omits Pi)
Theme count is 26, described as 'Twenty-six tinted-glass themes, from System to Catppuccin, Dracula, Claude and Codex'

Hydra pairing copy: 'a Claude lead over Gemini or OpenCode heads, picked straight from the model picker'; without a pair the heads take the chat's model at a working effort, so 'a Max lead sends out medium heads'
In a pair, the effort slider is the lead's and its track blends the lead's colour into the heads' (the slider alt text says 'its track blending the lead's orange into the heads' blue')
Panel docking limit stated as 'three a side on a 16-inch display, fewer on a smaller one'; panels can be dragged between slots to reorder or swap, and heads pop out on their own while there is room
The command palette shortcut is stated as the literal glyph CMD-K in 'Threads, projects and every command, from (CMD)K, over whatever you were doing.'

Plan limits are claimed for Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code and Z.ai; credits for DeepSeek and Command Code; Settings > Providers shows every signed-in provider on one page; the usage panel is switched on in General settings and can also be opened from the popover's expand button
API keys are needed only for DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai and are 'stored in your Keychain'; all other providers use the terminal session
Right-clicking the Hydra mark switches Hydra off for a chat
The welcome tour is 'Eight pages of real screenshots' and the Help menu reopens it
Checkpoints: 'After every turn Droppy Code records a hidden git checkpoint of your project', giving each reply a diff and a revert button, and a thread can be rewound to any earlier turn

The runtime behavior of data-morph-glyph, data-reveal-on-load, data-highlight-carousel/rail/slide/prev/next, data-theme-picker, data-wordsplit, data-binary-field and data-download-link is defined in site.js, code.js and wordscroll.js (not in this bundle); this file only declares the hooks and their initial attribute state.
/download/latest is a server-side redirect whose target artifact and host are not visible from this file.

The page advertises 10 agent providers while rendering 12 agent marks; whether the stat is stale or deliberately counts only a subset cannot be determined from this file.

files.purpose: The crawler policy served at https://getdroppycode.app/robots.txt. It opens the entire site to every user agent with no exclusions and points crawlers at the site's sitemap. Four lines, ASCII, CRLF line terminators.
calls_into: website/sitemap.xml, referenced by the absolute URL https://getdroppycode.app/sitemap.xml
platform_assumptions: None; a plain static text file with no macOS, AppKit or Unix dependency. It does hard-code the apex host getdroppycode.app.
feature_notes: Exact content line by line: line 1 'User-agent: *', line 2 'Allow: /', line 3 empty, line 4 'Sitemap: https://getdroppycode.app/sitemap.xml'
There is no Disallow directive and no Crawl-delay, so nothing on the site is excluded from indexing
There are no AI-crawler specific groups (no GPTBot, CCBot, ClaudeBot or similar sections): the single wildcard group covers everything
Every line uses CRLF terminators, matching the rest of the website directory
unresolved_questions: Whether the deploy pipeline rewrites the hard-coded host getdroppycode.app for preview or staging deployments cannot be determined from this file.
